newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B share index ends up on A shares.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B share index ends up on A shares.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended up on Monday but could not keep up with the sharp rises in the A shares which were pushed up by speculative buying as concerns about possible anti-speculative measures eased, brokers said.
The B index closed up 0.459 points or 0.65 percent to 70.898 points on volume of 20.2 million worth $8.2 million against $12 million last Friday.
The A share jumped 34.904 points or 2.96 percent to end at its year high of 1,212.753 points on volume of 1.1 billion shares worth 12 billion yuan, the heaviest trade in 1997.

Brokers said the A share market rose sharply on bullish sentiment with "hot money" (speculative funds) entering the market with investor concerns about possible measures to cool over-speculation easing.
They said the strong performance of the A share market also made investors unwilling to sell.
"The performance of the B share market is largely decided by domestic investors," one broker said.
"The index has already risen to a high level, and further rises will need an input of fresh overseas capital," a second broker said. "Otherwise the index will face a technical correction."
All 43 B shares traded, with 24 up, nine flat and 10 down.
Shanghai Dazhong Taxi Co was the star on speculative buying, jumping $0.082 or 8.40 percent to $1.058 on volume of 60,000 shares.
Shanghai Lianhua Fibre Co followed, rising $0.014 or 6.79 percent to $0.220 on volume of 29,000 shares.

Shanghai Diesel Engine Co traded the most on overseas unwinding selling on expectations of its unpromising 1996 results, but ended up on domestic institutional support late in the late session. It closed up $0.004 or 0.83 percent to $0.486 on volume of 2.6 million shares.
The SSE 30 blue-chip index jumped 155.213 points or 5.07 percent to 3,215.056 points.
Zhongshan Torch High & New Tech Industry Commercial Co was the star on speculative buying, surging 0.91 yuan or its daily limit-up of 10 percent to 9.97 yuan on volume of 11.2 million shares.
